Modern.positioningStatement: Home Later is a brokerage that works on the eighteen-month timeline most buyers actually live on.

Corporate.industrySummary: Commercial real estate advisory is a serious B2B category serving corporate occupiers, institutional investors, and large landlords. The category is dominated by the major brokerages (CBRE, JLL, Cushman) and a few specialist firms. Brand and discipline differentiate.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: CBRE (cbre.com) is the institutional giant. JLL (jll.com) holds the same tier. Cushman & Wakefield (cushmanwakefield.com) is the third major. Newmark (nmrk.com) sits closer in scale. We sit smaller and more focused on the mid-market commercial client.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Commercial property advisory for mid-market corporate occupiers and institutional investors.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Mid-market occupiers and investors are too small for the giants' attention and too sophisticated for boutique brokerages. We sit between them with operating depth and modern delivery.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: A common Irish surname plus the established category and a partner structure. Brennan reads as principal-led. Partners signals shared accountability. The pair feels like a regional brokerage with thirty years of records on file.
Corporate.manifesto: Brennan Realty Partners is a regional, full-service brokerage that handles residential and small-commercial transactions, plus ongoing property management. The work is unglamorous and steady. The team is mostly people who grew up here. The relationship outlasts the transaction.
Corporate.industrySummary: Mid-market regional brokerages are losing share to national platforms on the marketing side but holding on the management side. The opening is for a serious regional brand that competes on relationship and operational depth.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Coldwell Banker (coldwellbanker.com) is the national legacy reference. Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices (bhhs.com) is the peer. Local independents make up the floor. We sit in the regional principal-led slot with operational depth on management.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A principal-led regional brokerage with full-service property management — residential and small-commercial.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on tenure, local knowledge, and the depth of our management practice. The brokerage is the front door; the management practice is the building.

targetAudience.primary: Homeowners, small landlords, and small-commercial owners in our region — typically with a multi-decade horizon.
behaviors: Own two to twelve units.

Read the local paper.
motivations: Want one broker for the long arc — buying, leasing, managing, selling.

Send annual portfolio reviews.

Corporate.brandDescription: Lyndon Realty Holdings operates a portfolio of real-estate brokerage brands across residential, commercial, and property-management categories.
Corporate.scope:
Lyndon Realty Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand brokerage operations
• Shared marketing infrastructure and listing-platform integrations
• Property management for commercial and residential portfolios
• Real-estate finance and transaction coordination
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier real-estate brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A real-estate operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the marketing and finance infrastructure are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — marketing and transactions run on schedule.
Reliable — predictable operations across brokerages.
Discreet — brokerage relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Lyndon is a real American place-name with a heritage holding-company register. Realty Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in real estate (Realogy Holdings, Compass's holding structure, RE/MAX Holdings, Anywhere Real Estate structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Lyndon Realty Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of real-estate brokerage brands. Each brand retains its identity, agent leadership, and market relationships; we operate the shared marketing infrastructure, transaction coordination, and back office. The buyer is a brokerage founder considering sale, a developer seeking single-vendor brokerage relationships, or an institutional investor holding real-estate-services assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Real-estate brokerage has consolidated under a small number of large multi-brand operators (Realogy/Anywhere, RE/MAX, Compass). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep marketing infrastructure and the procurement-grade reliability developers and institutional investors require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Anywhere Real Estate (anywhere.re) is the multi-brand brokerage reference. RE/MAX Holdings (remax.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Compass (compass.com) sits in the modern multi-brokerage peer position. Howard Hanna (howardhanna.com) plays the regional multi-brand peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand brokerage operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Lyndon Realty Holdings is a regional multi-brand real-estate operator running brokerage, property management, and transaction coordination across a portfolio of independent brokerage brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared marketing infrastructure, transaction-coordination scale, and the procurement-grade reliability brokerage founders and institutional investors need.

targetAudience.primary: Brokerage founders considering sale, regional developers seeking single-vendor brokerage relationships, and institutional investors holding real-estate-services assets.
behaviors: Manage multi-brokerage operations.
Negotiate multi-year listing and development agreements.
Care about agent retention, transaction volume, and brokerage operations.
Renew on multi-year operating terms.
motivations: Need an operator with shared marketing.
Need to keep brand identity post-acquisition.
Need a single-vendor multi-brand brokerage relationship.

dos: Lead with brand portfolio, market footprint, and agent count.
Speak the language of brokerage founders, developers, and procurement.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to brokerages by name, not by Lyndon tagging.
donts: No social media at the parent level.
No brand consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

messagingPillars.name: Transaction coordination

Creative.tagline: A brokerage that draws the house before selling it.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Floorplan is the real architectural drawing of a property — a real trade-vocabulary noun. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most real estate brands sell move-in ready. The staged perfection. The finished surface. We made Good Bones because the most interesting homes aren't the polished ones. They are the houses with the original windows, the unfortunate kitchen, the staircase that creaks. The brand is for the buyers who can see what the house wants to be.
Creative.industrySummary: Real estate branding has been polished, staged, and slightly aspirational. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the imperfect houses that reward the patient buyer.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Cottages & Bungalows (cottagesandbungalowsmag.com) holds the heritage-home appreciation peer position. Curbed (curbed.com) does the design-led discovery middle. The Houseblog community sits in the restoration-led peer position. We sit warmer and more honest about the work.
Creative.positioningStatement: A real estate brand for buyers who can see past the carpet.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Looking for a first or second home. Has watched a renovation show. Wants the house with character, not the new build with a kitchen island.

dos: Tell the truth about the work
Photograph the house as it is, not staged
Talk like the friend who has restored a kitchen

Creative.tagline: A brokerage for the moment the house becomes home.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Doorstep is the real entry threshold of a house — the moment in every real-estate transaction. The definite article gives the brand the register of a small named firm.
Creative.manifesto: Most brokerages name themselves after grand things — estates, premier, prestige, summit. We made New Keys because the actual best part of the job is the day the buyer steps inside the empty house and the new keys are in their hand. That is the moment. We named the brand after it.
Creative.industrySummary: Real estate marketing trades in adjectives and aspiration. There is room for a brand that trades in the specific moment of the transaction — the doorstep, the keys, the first night. A brokerage that feels more like a documentary crew than a sales team.
Creative.competitorLandscape: @properties (atproperties.com) holds the modern-brand brokerage slot. Engel & Völkers (engelvoelkers.com) is the European-modern peer. Block Three Sixty (block360.com.au) plays in the warm-creative space. We are sharper and more specific — the moment, not the lifestyle.
Creative.positioningStatement: New Keys is a brokerage that documents the moment a house becomes a home — and works backwards from there.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand is the moment of the handover. Every other piece of the practice — marketing, photography, listing copy — is reverse-engineered from that frame.

targetAudience.primary: First and second-time buyers 28–45 who are buying a primary residence and want the process to feel human.
behaviors: Save photos of empty rooms with light coming in.
Read first-night-in-a-new-house essays.
Want a story to tell about how they bought it.
Care about the small ritual.
motivations: Want a brokerage that treats the purchase as personal.
Want photographs of the empty house, not the staged one.
Want the day to feel like something they will remember.

dos: Write in scenes — 'the kettle on the counter, the keys on the windowsill'.
Photograph the empty house at handover.
Send a small ritual gift on the move-in day.
Use first names throughout.

messagingPillars.name: The handover frame
messagingPillars.description: Every closed sale ends with a photograph of the keys on the kitchen counter of the empty house, taken by the agent. The image lives on the listing forever.

messagingPillars.name: The first night
messagingPillars.description: We send a small box on move-in day: a candle, a kettle, a folded note from the agent. It is the only marketing we do.

messagingPillars.name: Slow listings
messagingPillars.description: Every listing has a long-form scene-set written by the agent — what the house feels like at 7am, where the light comes from, what the kitchen smells like in winter.

Creative.tagline: A brokerage built around the showing.
Creative.brandDescription: The Showing Co is a creative-led brokerage that positions the property showing — the moment the buyer walks through the house — as the central experience of the transaction, with showings conducted as small considered events.
Creative.scope:
The Showing Co works across:
• Residential property showings positioned as considered events
• Buyer preparation programs before showings
• Documented showing notes for buyers after each visit
• Quarterly published essays on the showing tradition
• Annual property tours of the brokerage's notable past listings
Creative.mission: To restore the showing as the central moment of the real-estate transaction.
Creative.vision: A brokerage whose showing approach becomes a small cultural reference for what residential brokerage can be.
coreValues: Warm — the showing is the moment.
Specific — every showing has preparation and documentation.
Considered — the pace is unhurried.
Literary — the writing about showings is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Showing is the real-estate-trade word for an arranged property viewing — the moment the buyer walks through a house with the broker. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. Stands in the lineage of declarative-position brokerage brands.
Creative.manifesto: Most brokerage treats the showing as a rushed walkthrough. We started The Showing Co because the actual best brokerage moment is the showing — the buyer walking through the house, asking the questions, imagining the life. We treat showings as small considered events with preparation, documentation, and a slow pace.
Creative.industrySummary: Brokerage culture treats showings as efficiency-driven walkthroughs. There is real space for a creative-led brokerage that positions explicitly on the showing as the central experience, with preparation programs and documented follow-up.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Modern brokerages treat showings as transactional events. Most boutique brokerages emphasize listings, marketing, or agent relationships rather than showings as central experience. We sit further out — the showing is the brand.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Showing Co is a residential brokerage that positions the property showing as the central experience of the transaction, with showings conducted as considered events.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the showing premise. Every aspect of the brokerage — preparation programs, documentation, pace — is built around the showing.

targetAudience.primary: Considered residential buyers who view multiple properties before purchase and want the showing to be a serious experience.
behaviors: View 10-30 properties before deciding.
Take notes during property visits.
Care about understanding the house before deciding.
Want a brokerage that doesn't rush the visit.
motivations: Want showings as considered events.
Want preparation before and documentation after.
Want a brokerage that takes the showing seriously.

dos: Lead with the showing approach.
Publish the quarterly essay on the showing tradition.
Reference specific houses and showings in case material.
Sign correspondence by the showing broker.

messagingPillars.name: Considered showings
messagingPillars.description: Every showing is scheduled with adequate time. The broker prepares notes on the property in advance and walks through unhurried with the buyer.

messagingPillars.name: Preparation programs
messagingPillars.description: Before a showing, buyers receive a preparation document — questions to ask, things to notice, considerations for the property type. The preparation is the brokerage's gift.

messagingPillars.name: Documented follow-up
messagingPillars.description: After each showing, buyers receive a written follow-up — observations from the showing, answers to questions raised, next-step recommendations. The documentation is the relationship.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Showing Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a doorway beside it. The mark appears on showing documentation and brokerage correspondence.

colorPalette.name: Doorway
colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the colour of an oak doorway.

typography.primary: A quiet display serif for the wordmark and the quarterly essay.
typography.secondary: A book serif for showing documentation and buyer correspondence.
typography.rationale: Two related serifs. The brand reads like a small printed publication on residential brokerage.
